Subject: Post-demo: QuestWell performance qualification & next steps

Thanks again for the demo time today — great discussion and appreciate the signal into your production traffic shape. I wanted to capture the items we committed to and a short SLO checklist so we have a shared acceptance path.

High-level customer priorities (as we heard):
- Interactive doc ingestion + multi-turn assistant for support agents — low latency for typing/streaming experience is critical.
- Peak throughput during morning and evening shifts (short bursts).
- Cost sensitivity for settled scale (goal to optimize per-1M-token cost without giving up SLA guarantees).

SLO/qualification summary (please confirm these are accurate priorities):
- Latency: P95 generate <= 300 ms (95% of requests), target. P99 target <= 800 ms (grace).
- Streaming: first-token to client <= 200 ms for small responses (<= 64 tokens); steady-state chunking latency <= 100 ms preferred.
- Throughput: baseline sustained 120 QPS, burst capacity up to 350 QPS for <2m windows.
- Concurrency: typical active concurrency ~12-16 handlers; allow headroom to 32 during ramp.
- Availability: 99.95% regional SLA, fallback to lower-cost variant if regional capacity constrained.

Proposed next steps (action items):
1) QuestWell: share 2 representative payloads (short assistant flow + larger context flow) and a daily traffic profile CSV (hourly QPS) — attached sample payloads.
2) Redwood: run a joint staged load test in your staging environment against our staging endpoint, then run a production-readiness soak in our dedicated pool.
3) Technical sync: schedule 60m with Priyom to agree on model variants, quantization profile, and KV cache sizing.
4) Decision criteria: we recommend acceptance if P95 <= 350ms and throughputs meet 90% of target sustained for a 10-minute window with no >5% error rate.

Attachments: [Attachment: questwell_sample_payloads.json (application/json)], [Attachment: post-demo-perf-matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

Let us know if the SLOs above look right; if yes, Priyom will follow up with a technical plan and proposed test windows. If there are any additional constraints (e.g., certs, IP allowlist), flag them here so we include them in the runbook.

Thanks,
Ben

Thanks — looping in a proposed technical test plan below (high level). I can walk through this during the sync; please comment with any constraints.

Proposed test plan (staging -> canary -> dedicated):
- Phase 0 (prep): exchange certs, IP allowlist, and test credentials. Validate payloads in a 10-minute functional run (no load).
- Phase 1 (staging spike): 10m ramp to 150 QPS against our inference-staging.redwood.internal endpoint. Model: redwood-*-v2 (quantized int8) — we'll share exact variant. Metrics to capture: P50/P95/P99 latency, error rate, token throughput, streaming first-byte latency.
- Phase 2 (canary soak): 30m sustain at 120 QPS with 16 concurrency. Validate KV cache hit-rate and observe tail latencies under warmed cache.
- Phase 3 (dedicated soak): 60m at 120 QPS sustained and three 2-minute bursts to 350 QPS to validate autoscaling/queueing behavior.
- Failure criteria: >5% errors, P99 > 1.2s, sustained P95 > 500ms. In that case we stop and iterate.

Infra notes:
- We'll provide a small load harness (skeleton attached: loadtest-plan.sh) and an optional JMeter plan if you prefer.
- For streaming verification we'll run a websocket-based harness that measures first-byte and steady-state chunk delivery.

Schedule: I have availability Thurs/Fri this week 9-11am PT for the tech sync.
